artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be an infinite-dimensional uniformly convex Banach space. (Recall that $X$ is uniformly convex if for every $\varepsilon\in(0,2]$ there exists $\delta>0$ such that for all $x,y\in X$ with $\|x\|=\|y\|=1$ and $\|x-y\|\ge\varepsilon$ one has $\|(x+y)/2\|\le 1-\delta$.) For finite-dimensional Banach spaces $E,F$ of the same dimension, write $d(E,F)=\inf\{\|T\|\cdot\|T^{-1}\|:T:E\to F\ \text{linear isomorphism}\}$ for the Banach–Mazur distance, and let $\ell_2^n$ denote $n$-dimensional Hilbert space.

Question: Does there exist a constant $C=C(X)<\infty$ such that for every positive integer $n$ there exist a subspace $Y_n\subseteq X$ and a bounded linear projection $P_n:X\to Y_n$ satisfying
$$d(Y_n,\ell_2^n)\le C\qquad\text{and}\qquad \|P_n\|\le C\,?$$
artifact.status_search_result: A direct search did not reveal a definitive resolution of this specific question for general infinite-dimensional uniformly convex Banach spaces. Related results (Lindenstrauss–Tzafriri, K-convexity, Pisier's work on projection constants and Hilbertian subspaces) provide partial information, but the uniform-in-$n$ existence of well-complemented finite-dimensional subspaces uniformly close to $\ell_2^n$ inside every uniformly convex space appears to remain unresolved based on the available evidence.

status_evidence.title: A Survey on the Complemented Subspace Problem
status_evidence.snippet: Problems related to complemented subspaces are in the heart of the theory of Banach spaces; these are more than fifty years old and play a key role in development of the theory.
status_evidence.claim: The complemented subspace problem and related questions about complemented Hilbertian subspaces remain active research areas.

status_evidence.title: Projections onto Hilbertian subspaces of Banach spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Estimates for the relative projection constants of Hilbertian subspaces in Banach spaces in terms of geometrical properties of the space.
status_evidence.claim: Related quantitative bounds on projections onto Hilbertian subspaces are known but do not directly settle the uniform-constant question for general uniformly convex spaces.
